questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

class TextSession(BrowserSession):
    """A BrowserSession that never captures screenshots for the step state (browser-use always asks for one).
    In the sandbox, screenshots of the run's browsers stalled the page-state capture for 30 s per step."""

    async def get_browser_state_summary(self, include_screenshot: bool = True, cached: bool = False,
                                        include_recent_events: bool = False):
        return await super().get_browser_state_summary(include_screenshot=False, cached=cached,
                                                       include_recent_events=include_recent_events)


def make_session(ctx, browser: int = 0, vision: bool = False) -> BrowserSession:
    """Attach to the run's CDP browser `browser` (locally browser-use starts its own Chromium; HEADLESS=1 hides it)."""
    urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
    cls = BrowserSession if vision else TextSession
    profile = dict(allowed_domains=allowed_domains(ctx.task), enable_default_extensions=False, keep_alive=True)
    if urls:
        return cls(cdp_url=urls[browser % len(urls)], **profile)
    return cls(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1", window_size={"width": 1280, "height": 800}, **profile)


async def _evaluate(browser_session: BrowserSession, js: str, *args):
    page = await browser_session.must_get_current_page()
    raw = await page.evaluate(js, *args)
    try:
        return json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw[:1] in ("[", "{") else raw
    except ValueError:
        return raw


async def read_current_page(browser_session: BrowserSession) -> str:
    """Full text of the current page (see swarm.page_text). Retries while the page is still loading."""
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            return clean(str(await _evaluate(browser_session, EXTRACT_JS, {})))
        except Exception as error:   # page navigating / not ready yet
            if attempt == 3:
                raise
            log.debug("read retry: %s", error)
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
    return ""


def _same_site(url: str, current: str, task: dict) -> str | None:
    full = urljoin(current, url)
    host = f"{urlparse(full).scheme}://{urlparse(full).netloc}"
    return full if host in allowed_domains(task) else None


async def browse(ctx, goal: str, *, browser: int = 0, site_id: str = "", on_record=None, max_steps: int = 40,
                 hints: str = "", author: str = "browse", use_vision=False, stop_reserve: float | None = None,
                 extra_tools=None, max_actions_per_step: int = 4) -> dict:
    """Run a browser-use agent until done / max_steps / out of time. Returns {"summary", "records", "steps", "done"}.

    Screenshots are off by default (`use_vision=False`): capturing them hung in the sandbox browsers, and `read_page`
    already reads canvas labels and hidden text. `stop_reserve`: stop when the run has this many seconds left
    (default: the SUBMIT reserve). `extra_tools(tools)`
    may register more actions. Pages read with a `topic` reach `on_record` as {"kind": "page", "data": {...}}.
    """
    records: list[dict] = []
    reserve = SUBMIT_RESERVE_S if stop_reserve is None else stop_reserve

    async def emit(rec: dict) -> None:
        records.append(rec)
        if on_record:
            await on_record(rec)

    tools = build_tools(ctx, site_id, author, emit)
    if extra_tools:
        extra_tools(tools)

    session = make_session(ctx, browser, vision=bool(use_vision))
    agent = Agent(task=goal, llm=make_llm(), browser_session=session, tools=tools, use_vision=use_vision,
                  use_judge=False, generate_gif=False, max_failures=6, max_actions_per_step=max_actions_per_step,
                  llm_timeout=150, step_timeout=240,
                  extend_system_message=SYSTEM_EXTRA + (f"\n{hints}" if hints else ""))

    async def stop_when_out_of_time(_agent) -> None:
        if ctx.seconds_left() <= reserve:
            agent.stop()

    try:
        history = await agent.run(max_steps=max_steps, on_step_start=stop_when_out_of_time)
    finally:
        await session.kill() if not browsers.cdp_urls() else await session.stop()   # never kill the run's browsers
    return {"summary": history.final_result() or "", "records": records, "steps": len(history.history),
            "done": history.is_done()}

						self.logger.debug(f'Reusing existing about:blank tab #{target_id[-4:]}')
						break

				# Create new tab if no reusable one found
				if not target_id:
					self.logger.debug('[on_NavigateToUrlEvent] No reusable about:blank tab found, creating new tab...')
					try:
						target_id = await self._cdp_create_new_page('about:blank')
						self.logger.debug(f'Created new tab #{target_id[-4:]}')
						# Dispatch TabCreatedEvent for new tab
						await self.event_bus.dispatch(TabCreatedEvent(target_id=target_id, url='about:blank'))
					except Exception as e:
						self.logger.error(f'[on_NavigateToUrlEvent] Failed to create new tab: {type(e).__name__}: {e}')
						# Fall back to using current tab
						target_id = current_target_id
						self.logger.warning(f'[on_NavigateToUrlEvent] Falling back to current tab #{target_id[-4:]}')
			else:
				# Use current tab
				target_id = target_id or current_target_id

			# Switch to target tab if needed (for both new_tab=True and new_tab=False)
			if self.agent_focus_target_id is None or self.agent_focus_target_id != target_id:
				self.logger.debug(
					f'[on_NavigateToUrlEvent] Switching to target tab {target_id[-4:]} (current: {self.agent_focus_target_id[-4:] if self.agent_focus_target_id else "none"})'
				)
				# Activate target (bring to foreground)
				await self.event_bus.dispatch(SwitchTabEvent(target_id=target_id))
			else:
				self.logger.debug(f'[on_NavigateToUrlEvent] Already on target tab {target_id[-4:]}, skipping SwitchTabEvent')

			assert self.agent_focus_target_id is not None and self.agent_focus_target_id == target_id, (
				'Agent focus not updated to new target_id after SwitchTabEvent should have switched to it'
			)

			# Dispatch navigation started
			await self.event_bus.dispatch(NavigationStartedEvent(target_id=target_id, url=event.url))

			# Navigate to URL with proper lifecycle waiting
			await self._navigate_and_wait(event.url, target_id, wait_until=event.wait_until)

			# Close any extension options pages that might have opened
			await self._close_extension_options_pages()

			# Dispatch navigation complete
			self.logger.debug(f'Dispatching NavigationCompleteEvent for {event.url} (tab #{target_id[-4:]})')
			await self.event_bus.dispatch(
				NavigationCompleteEvent(
					target_id=target_id,
					url=event.url,
					status=None,  # CDP doesn't provide status directly
				)
			)
			await self.event_bus.dispatch(AgentFocusChangedEvent(target_id=target_id, url=event.url))

			# Note: These should be handled by dedicated watchdogs:
			# - Security checks (security_watchdog)
			# - Page health checks (crash_watchdog)
			# - Dialog handling (dialog_watchdog)
			# - Download handling (downloads_watchdog)
			# - DOM rebuilding (dom_watchdog)

		except Exception as e:
			self.logger.error(f'Navigation failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}')
			# target_id might be unbound if exception happens early
			if 'target_id' in locals() and target_id:
				await self.event_bus.dispatch(
					NavigationCompleteEvent(
						target_id=target_id,
						url=event.url,
						error_message=f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}',
					)
				)
				await self.event_bus.dispatch(AgentFocusChangedEvent(target_id=target_id, url=event.url))
			raise

	async def _navigate_and_wait(
		self,
		url: str,
		target_id: str,
		timeout: float | None = None,
		wait_until: str = 'load',
	) -> None:
		"""Navigate to URL and wait for page readiness using CDP lifecycle events.

		Polls stored lifecycle events (registered once per session in SessionManager).
		wait_until controls the minimum acceptable signal: 'commit', 'domcontentloaded', 'load', 'networkidle'.
		"""
		cdp_session = await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=False)

		if timeout is None:
			target = self.session_manager.get_target(target_id)
			current_url = target.url
			same_domain = (
				url.split('/')[2] == current_url.split('/')[2]
				if url.startswith('http') and current_url.startswith('http')
				else False
			)
			timeout = 3.0 if same_domain else 8.0

		nav_start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()

		# Wrap Page.navigate() with timeout — heavy sites can block here for 10s+
		nav_timeout = 20.0
		try:
			nav_result = await asyncio.wait_for(
				cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Page.navigate(
					params={'url': url, 'transitionType': 'address_bar'},
					session_id=cdp_session.session_id,
				),
				timeout=nav_timeout,
			)
		except TimeoutError:
			duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
			raise RuntimeError(f'Page.navigate() timed out after {nav_timeout}s ({duration_ms:.0f}ms) for {url}')

		if nav_result.get('errorText'):
			raise RuntimeError(f'Navigation failed: {nav_result["errorText"]}')

		if wait_until == 'commit':
			duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
			self.logger.debug(f'✅ Page ready for {url} (commit, {duration_ms:.0f}ms)')
			return

		navigation_id = nav_result.get('loaderId')
		start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
		seen_events = []

		if not hasattr(cdp_session, '_lifecycle_events'):
			raise RuntimeError(
				f'❌ Lifecycle monitoring not enabled for {cdp_session.target_id[:8]}! '
				f'This is a bug - SessionManager should have initialized it. '
				f'Session: {cdp_session}'
			)

		# Acceptable events by readiness level (higher is always acceptable)
		acceptable_events: set[str] = {'networkIdle'}
		if wait_until in ('load', 'domcontentloaded'):
			acceptable_events.add('load')
		if wait_until == 'domcontentloaded':
			acceptable_events.add('DOMContentLoaded')

		poll_interval = 0.05
		while (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start_time) < timeout:
			try:
				for event_data in list(cdp_session._lifecycle_events):
					event_name = event_data.get('name')
					event_loader_id = event_data.get('loaderId')

					event_str = f'{event_name}(loader={event_loader_id[:8] if event_loader_id else "none"})'
					if event_str not in seen_events:
						seen_events.append(event_str)

					if event_loader_id and navigation_id and event_loader_id != navigation_id:
						continue

					if event_name in acceptable_events:
						duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
						self.logger.debug(f'✅ Page ready for {url} ({event_name}, {duration_ms:.0f}ms)')
						return

			except Exception as e:
				self.logger.debug(f'Error polling lifecycle events: {e}')

			await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)

		duration_ms = (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - nav_start_time) * 1000
		if not seen_events:
			self.logger.error(
				f'❌ No lifecycle events received for {url} after {duration_ms:.0f}ms! '
				f'Monitoring may have failed. Target: {cdp_session.target_id[:8]}'
			)
		else:
			self.logger.warning(f'⚠️ Page readiness timeout ({timeout}s, {duration_ms:.0f}ms) for {url}')

	async def on_SwitchTabEvent(self, event: SwitchTabEvent) -> TargetID:
		"""Handle tab switching - core browser functionality."""
		if not self.agent_focus_target_id:
			raise RuntimeError('Cannot switch tabs - browser not connected')

"""Browsers for agents. In a run: CDP browsers 1-4 from the sandbox (never launch your own). Locally: one Chromium."""
import browsers


class BrowserPool:
    def __init__(self, REDACTED):
        self._pw = REDACTED
        self._contexts: dict[int, object] = {}   # slot -> browser context

    async def context(self, index: int = 0):
        n = len(browsers.cdp_urls())
        slot = index % n if n else 0             # locally everything shares one Chromium
        if slot not in self._contexts:
            _, page = await browsers.connect(self._pw, slot)
            self._contexts[slot] = page.context
        return self._contexts[slot]

    async def new_page(self, index: int = 0):
        """A fresh tab in browser `index`; tabs are unlimited, browsers are not (max 4)."""
        return await (await self.context(index)).new_page()
"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run REDACTED install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(REDACTED, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page

starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run REDACTED install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(REDACTED, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await REDACTED.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page

"""Model-driven browsing via the browser-use framework. The MODEL decides where to go and what matters; browser-use gives
it hands and eyes. This module only wires it to our setup: the run's CDP browsers, the Qwen proxy, no telemetry, navigation
limited to the task's websites, and three actions of our own:

- `read_page`: extract the full text of the page the model chose (iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips, canvas labels),
  optionally open a URL first and follow a "next page" link the model names; with a `topic` the text is kept as evidence.
- `record`: save one fact the model read.
- `fill_form`: set several fields of the current form at once (helper for long forms such as the bid configurator).

    out = await browse(ctx, goal="...", browser=1, site_id="erp", on_record=callback)

Rule: ONE browse() at a time per browser index (an agent works in the browser's active tab). Use different indices (0-3)
for parallel agents. Per-site knowledge goes into `goal`/`hints` as general strategy, never scenario values.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

# No telemetry / cloud sync / version check: the sandbox may only talk to the platform and the four sites.
for _flag in ("ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY", "BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC", "BROWSER_USE_VERSION_CHECK"):
    os.environ[_flag] = "false"
os.environ.setdefault("BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL", "info")
# The sandbox browsers are slower than a laptop: give page-state capture more time before browser-use calls it a failure.
os.environ.setdefault("TIMEOUT_BrowserStateRequestEvent", "60")
os.environ.setdefault("TIMEOUT_NavigateToUrlEvent", "45")

from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, BrowserProfile, BrowserSession, ChatOpenAI, Tools  # noqa: E402,F401
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field  # noqa: E402

import browsers  # noqa: E402
import models  # noqa: E402
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S  # noqa: E402
from swarm.page_text import EXTRACT_JS, NEXT_JS, clean  # noqa: E402

log = logging.getLogger("browse")

PAGE_TEXT_LIMIT = 12_000      # characters of one read the model sees (the saved evidence keeps up to 10x more)

SYSTEM_EXTRA = """
Working rules:
- Dismiss cookie walls, surveys and popups (close them; do not follow their links). If a session expired or you see a
  login form again, log in again (credentials are in the task). Retry error pages ("erneut versuchen") a few times.
- Use `read_page` to read a page: it returns ALL text including iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips and canvas labels,

"""The swarm framework against fakes: blackboard, JSON parsing, phase orchestration, failure isolation."""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from swarm import Agent, Blackboard, Evidence, Phase  # noqa: E402
from swarm import orchestrator  # noqa: E402
from swarm.llm import parse_json  # noqa: E402

TASK = {"brief": "b", "access": [{"siteId": "erp", "url": "http://x", "credentials": {}}],
        "submission": {"kind": "api"}, "expires_at": None}


class BoardTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_post_query_and_wait(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        waiter = asyncio.create_task(board.wait_for(kind="a.b", timeout=2))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        await board.post(Evidence("a.b", "erp", {"x": 1}, source="u"))
        self.assertEqual((await waiter)[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(board.query("a", prefix=True)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(board.query("a.b", site="mail"), [])

    async def test_dump_and_load_round_trip(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        await board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {"x": 1}))
        await board.set("r", [1])
        path = Path(__file__).parent / "_board.json"
        try:
            board.dump(path)
            again = Blackboard.load(path)
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(again.evidence[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(again.get("r"), [1])


class ParseJson(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fenced_and_chatty(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_json('Sure!\n```json\n{"a": [1, 2]}\n```'), {"a": [1, 2]})

    def test_garbage_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_json("no json here")


def make_agents(order):
    class Boom(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self): raise RuntimeError("boom")

    class Collect(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("collect")
            await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {}))

    class Analyze(Agent):
        phase = Phase.ANALYZE
        async def run(self):
            order.append(f"analyze sees {len(self.ctx.board.query('k'))}")

    class Submit(Agent):
        phase = Phase.SUBMIT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("submit")
            await self.ctx.board.set("answer", {"ok": True})

    return [Submit, Analyze, Boom, Collect]


class Orchestration(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_with(self, classes, task=TASK, env=None):
        with patch.object(orchestrator, "discover", lambda: classes):
            return await orchestrator.run_swarm(task, None, scored=True, env=env or {})

    async def test_phases_run_in_order_and_a_failure_does_not_stop_the_rest(self):
        order = []
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order))
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "analyze sees 1", "submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    async def test_site_submission_returns_nothing_to_post(self):
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents([]), task={**TASK, "submission": {"kind": "site"}})
        self.assertIsNone(answer)

    async def test_only_filter(self):
        order = []
        await self.run_with(make_agents(order), env={"SWARM_ONLY": "Collect,Submit"})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "submit"])

    async def test_out_of_time_skips_work_but_still_submits(self):
        order = []
        late = {**TASK, "expires_at": (time.time() + 100) * 1000}   # inside the submit margin
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order), task=late)
        self.assertEqual(order, ["submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})


class BrowserUseWiring(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_only_task_sites_are_allowed_and_telemetry_is_off(self):
        import os
        from swarm import browser_agent
        task = {"access": [{"url": "https://a.example/x?y=1"}, {"url": "http://b.example:8080/"}, {"url": ""}]}
        self.assertEqual(browser_agent.allowed_domains(task), ["https://a.example", "http://b.example:8080"])
        for flag in ("ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY", "BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC", "BROWSER_USE_VERSION_CHECK"):
            self.assertEqual(os.environ[flag], "false")


class BrowseTools(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_our_actions_are_registered_and_helpers_are_not(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        tools = browser_agent.build_tools(None, "erp", "t", None)
        names = set(tools.registry.registry.actions)
        self.assertTrue({"record", "read_page", "fill_form"} <= names)
        self.assertNotIn("read_one", names)


class RealAgentsImport(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_agent_module_imports_and_registers(self):
        names = {c.__name__ for c in orchestrator.discover()}
        self.assertTrue({"TenderScraper", "SpecScraper", "ErpScraper", "MailScraper", "BidSubmitter"} <= names)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    if answer is None:
        print("Nothing to post: the bid is entered and signed on the website by the submitter agent"
              if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else "No answer was produced", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

# Swarm guide

One process, one asyncio loop, many agents. Agents share a **blackboard**; the **orchestrator** runs them in phases.
Each person owns **one file in `agents/`** (no merge conflicts); shared code is in `swarm/` (change it by PR, small).

```
COLLECT (dataflow: scrapers + analysts, synchronised by done flags)  ->  VERIFY  ->  COMPUTE (plain code)  ->  SUBMIT
 scrapers save pages the MODEL chose; analysts turn them into results                                        enter bid, sign TAN
```

## Data flow (who waits for what)

```
BriefReader ──> results["brief"] (reference, scenario date, bidder, authorised senders), results["sites"] (role -> siteId)
TenderScraper (b0) ──tender.page──> done.tender ──> QuantityAnalyzer ──> results["tender"], results["quantities"]
SpecScraper   (b1) ──spec.page───> done.spec ───> RequirementAnalyzer ──> results["spec"], results["requirements"]
                                                        (+ Q&A amendments) ──> results["requirements_final"]
ErpScraper    (b2) waits results["requirements"] -> queue of catalogue groups; ErpHelper (b1) joins after done.spec
                   ──erp.page──> done.erp ──> MaterialMatcher ──> results["erp"], results["materials"]
MailScraper   (b3) pass 1 approvals/conditions/technical ──> done.mail_core, pass 2 other release mails ──> done.mail
                   ──mail.page──> DiscountAnalyzer ──> results["discount"], results["mail"], results["mailbox"]
EvidenceVerifier ──> results["verification"];  BidCalculator ──> results["bid"], results["answer"]
BidSubmitter (b0; TAN via a short browse on b3) ──> results["submission"]
```

Every scraper sets its `done.<role>` flag in a `finally`, so analysts never wait forever; every wait has a timeout
bounded by `ctx.time_left()`. Missing inputs degrade the bid (omitted positions, blank breakdown fields), never crash it.

## Files

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `swarm/blackboard.py` | `Evidence(kind, site, data, source, author, note)`, `Blackboard` (post/query/set/get/wait_for/dump/load) |
| `swarm/agent.py` | `Agent` base, `Phase`, `@register` |
| `swarm/context.py` | `ctx`: `task`, `board`, `llm`, `pool`, `site(id)`, `brief`, `time_left()`, `seconds_left()`, `lock(name)`, `shared` |
| `swarm/llm.py` | `ctx.llm.chat / ask / ask_json` (Qwen, concurrency-limited, usage counted), `parse_json` |
| `swarm/browser_agent.py` | `browse(ctx, goal, browser=n, ...)`: **browser-use** on our CDP browser + Qwen, with our actions `read_page`, `record`, `fill_form` |
| `swarm/page_text.py` | the page extractor behind `read_page` (iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips, canvas labels, zero-width chars) |
| `swarm/forms.py` | the form filler behind `fill_form` (cascading selects via an apply button) |
| `swarm/extract.py` | analyst helpers: saved pages -> model extraction with a JSON shape (chunked, merged) |
| `swarm/normalize.py` | numbers (de-DE/en-US), dates (MM/DD vs DD/MM, ISO), references, German display format, cent rounding |
| `swarm/sites.py` | role -> siteId mapping (site names differ per dataset) |
| `swarm/scraper.py` | `SiteScraper`: set `role`, `browser`, write `goal()`; `self.browse(job)` for extra passes |
| `swarm/orchestrator.py` | discovery of `agents/*`, phases, timeouts, failure isolation, board dumps |
| `agents/*.py` | the agents. Header comment of each file: OWNER / ROLE / NEEDS / WRITES and the result shapes |

## How the model browses

The model (Qwen via browser-use) decides where to go. Three actions of ours make it fast and exact:

- `read_page(url?, topic?, next_page_link?)`: full text of the page it chose (hidden-but-real content included,
  decoys hidden from people excluded); with `next_page_link` it reads every page of a paged list; with `topic` the
  text is saved as Evidence `"<role>.page"` for the analysts. This is "extract a selected page / paginate a
  model-selected result set" from the rules: the model selects, the helper extracts.
- `record(kind, data, source, note)`: one fact.
- `fill_form(fields, apply_button?, then_click?)`: many fields of a form in one step (bid configurator).

Analysts then ask the model to extract a JSON shape from the saved text (`swarm/extract.py`) and apply the brief's
rules in code (latest dated record wins, withdrawn answers ignored, exact reference, authorised sender, ...).

## Contracts (agree before changing)

Evidence kinds: `<role>.page` (data: topic, url, title, pages, text) for saved pages; `record` kinds as the scraper's
goal names them (e.g. `mail.tan`). Results keys and shapes are documented at the top of each agent file.
Done flags: `done.tender`, `done.spec`, `done.erp`, `done.mail_core`, `done.mail`, `requirements_final`, `mail_final`.

## Local development

```powershell
atira models proxy                                   # terminal 1
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression   # terminal 2
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # whole swarm; dumps .swarm/board.json after each phase
$env:SWARM_DEADLINE_S="1200"                         # optional: simulate the 20-minute clock locally
$env:SWARM_ONLY="MaterialMatcher,BidCalculator"; $env:SWARM_BOARD_IN=".swarm/board.json"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # only these agents, on a saved board (no re-scraping)
uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```
`SWARM_BOARD_IN` is ignored in scored runs. `.swarm/` holds scouting data: git-ignored, never ship it.
Replaying analysts on a saved board: the done flags are in the board, so waits return immediately.

## Time budget (20-minute run)

`SUBMIT_RESERVE_S` (default 540 s, env `SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S`): collecting/analysing stops that long before expiry,
then VERIFY/COMPUTE (instant) and SUBMIT, which stops `FINAL_MARGIN_S` (40 s) before expiry.

## Fair-play rules for everyone (a reviewer reads the package)

- No scenario values anywhere (prices, material numbers, refs, logins, TANs, totals, dates, keys, transaction codes):
  not in prompts, hints, defaults, tests or notes. Tests use invented dummy data. Strategy is fine, values are not.
- The model decides where to go and what matters. Code may parse, page through model-selected results, validate,
  compute, fill forms. No fixed click paths, URL lists, or crawl-everything-then-one-prompt helpers.
- Only the provided CDP browsers; no extra Chromium; no hosts besides the platform and the 4 sites; models via the proxy.
- Do not write comments addressed to the reviewer.

## Robustness settings (learned from the first sandbox runs)

- No screenshots per step (`TextSession`): in the sandbox they stalled every step for 30 s. `read_page` covers canvas text.
- Qwen's separate reasoning pass is off and replies are forced to a JSON object (`QwenChat`, `LLM.ask_json`): steps
  went from 10-75 s to a few seconds and the "invalid JSON / prose reply" failures stop.
- Scrapers, ERP items and the submitter retry an agent that stopped early, telling it what is already saved.
- Requirements are published early (as soon as a requirement table page is saved) so the ERP work starts sooner.

## Work split (3 people) and how to iterate on your part

| Person | Agents | Iterate with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: tender + spec | `scrape_tender`, `scrape_spec`, `analyze_quantities`, `analyze_requirements` | `SWARM_ONLY=TenderScraper,QuantityAnalyzer` live; analysts on a saved board |
| B: ERP | `scrape_erp` (ErpScraper, ErpHelper), `analyze_materials` | `SWARM_ONLY=ErpScraper,MaterialMatcher` on a board that has `requirements` |
| C: mail + shared | `scrape_mail`, `analyze_discount`, `compute_bid`, `submit_bid`, `swarm/*` | analysts/calculator on a saved board; `tests/test_rules.py` |

Loop: run your scraper live once -> it dumps `.swarm/board.json` -> replay your analyst on it as often as needed
(`SWARM_BOARD_IN`) -> check the result keys -> tune the goal/hints (strategy only) or the extraction shape -> repeat.
Then a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) to check timing; debug with `atira logs <run>`.

## Open items

- Tune goals/hints per site from test-run logs (`atira` MCP: `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_screenshot`).
- Submitter: watch the first real runs closely (wizard order, TAN timing).
- Cost: browser-use sends the goal every step; keep goals short.

lastPrompt: The tender portal agent is always stuck and does not spin up. What is the cause [Image #1]of it?

content.text:
The tender agent never started because browser-use's own loading screen blocked the first page load in that browser. I've patched it and started a new test run (`run_6d23d89bb0e28366`) to check the fix in the sandbox.

**What your screenshot shows.** The tab titled "Starting agent c63e…" with the black screen is browser-use's loading animation. It draws a logo picture loaded from `cf.browser-use.com`. The sandbox can only reach the platform and the four sites, so that request never answers. You can see it in the screenshot: the broken image box, and the stop (✕) button meaning the tab is still loading.

**What the logs show.** In `run_354961221455dd45`:
- The tender agent tried to open the tender portal for about 10 minutes. Every attempt failed with `Page.navigate() timed out after 20.0s`, and the tab stayed on about:blank.
- When it tried to change the page with JavaScript instead, that step hung for the full 240 s.
- The portal itself answers in about 0.2 s, and the other three browsers navigated normally at the same time. So the problem is that one tab, not the site.
- The same symptom showed up in an earlier run (`run_4dee…`). In `run_53dd…` the tender agent reached the site and collected the bidder questions, so it doesn't happen every time.

I'm fairly sure of the cause but haven't proven it in the sandbox yet; I'll know once this run reaches the tender portal. The animation also contacts a host outside the allowed list, which the fair-play rules forbid, so it has to go regardless.

**What I changed (`swarm/browser_agent.py`):**
1. Turned off the loading animation, so about:blank tabs load nothing from outside.
2. Added `RobustSession`, which `TextSession` now builds on: if a navigation still hangs, it stops the stuck load and retries once.
3. Added a test that the animation is off. I also changed one message in `agent.py` so an existing starter-kit test passes again. All 42 tests pass.
4. Added a note to `docs/SWARM.md`. This was saved after the upload, so the test run doesn't include it; it doesn't affect behaviour.

Locally, the patched browser opens the tender portal login page in 0.6 s.

**Test runs.** I cancelled `run_354961221455dd45`, because its tender agent could no longer recover and no bid was possible. A watch on the new run reports navigation timeouts and the main milestones.

**Local check of the ERP and analysis steps.** It's still running:
- The discount comes out at 5%, with 9 of 14 messages accepted as valid.
- The ERP agent is slow: it used about 25 steps for one catalogue group. This is the next thing to fix once the tender step works in the sandbox.

Nothing is committed or submitted.

def test_index_window_and_newest_key_wins(self):
        msgs = [{"topic": "price_indices", "date": "2031-01-01", "entries": [
                    {"index": "IX", "eur_per_kg": 1.5, "valid_from": "01.12.2030", "valid_to": "31.01.2031"},
                    {"index": "IX", "eur_per_kg": 2.5, "valid_from": "01.02.2031", "valid_to": None}]},
                {"topic": "packaging_tariffs", "date": "2031-01-01", "entries": [{"key": "P-1", "eur_per_carton": 9}]},
                {"topic": "packaging_tariffs", "date": "2031-01-02", "entries": [{"key": "P-1", "eur_per_carton": 11}]}]
        mail = summarise(msgs, to_datetime("2031-01-31T12:00:00Z"))
        self.assertEqual(mail["price_indices"]["IX"], "1.5")
        self.assertEqual(mail["packaging_tariffs"]["P-1"], "11")


class Pricing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scale_validity_and_allocation(self):
        cond = [{"material": "M-1", "valid_from": "01.01.2031", "valid_to": "31.03.2031, 23:59:59 UTC",
                 "price_unit": "10", "number_format": "en-US",
                 "scales": [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "1,000.00"}, {"min_qty": "20", "price": "900.00"}]}]
        c = valid_condition(cond, "M-1", to_datetime("2031-03-31T12:00:00Z"))
        self.assertEqual(scale_price(c, 19), Decimal("100"))
        self.assertEqual(scale_price(c, 20), Decimal("90"))
        self.assertIsNone(valid_condition(cond, "M-1", to_datetime("2031-04-01T00:00:01Z")))
        self.assertEqual(allocate_cents(Decimal("1.00"), {"a": Decimal(1), "b": Decimal(1), "c": Decimal(1)}),
                         {"a": Decimal("0.34"), "b": Decimal("0.33"), "c": Decimal("0.33")})
        self.assertEqual(marginal_bonus(Decimal("150"), [{"from": "0", "to": "100", "percent": "0"},
                                                         {"from": "100", "to": None, "percent": "10"}]), Decimal("5.00"))

    def test_full_bid(self):
        inputs = {
            "brief": {"tender_reference": "T-9", "scenario_date": "2031-02-01T09:00:00Z"},
            "tender": {"positions": [{"position": "1", "quantity": "4", "unit": "Stk", "requirement_ref": "Z-1"},
                                     {"position": "2", "quantity": "2", "unit": "Satz", "requirement_ref": "Z-2"}],
                       "clarifications": [{"number": "5", "date": "2031-01-01", "positions": ["1"], "setup_fee": "10,00 EUR",
                                           "keys": {"konditionsgruppe": "K-1", "packaging_tariff": "P-1"}}]},
            "quantities": {"1": {"quantity": 4}, "2": {"quantity": 2}},
            "requirements": {"Z-1": {}, "Z-2": {"pieces_per_set": "3"}},
            "materials": {"1": {"material": "M-1"}, "2": {"material": "M-1"}},
            "erp": {"materials": {"M-1": {"pieces_per_carton": "3", "surcharge_mass_g": "500", "metal_index": "IX",
                                          "lead_time_stock_weeks": "2", "lead_time_production_weeks": "8"}},
                    "conditions": [{"material": "M-1", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31",
                                    "price_unit": "1", "currency": "EUR", "scales": [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "100.00"}]}],
                    "stock": {"M-1": {"free": "10"}}},
            "discount": {"percent": "10", "min_order_value": "500"},
            "mail": {"condition_rules": {"K-1": "base_and_surcharge"}, "packaging_tariffs": {"P-1": "6"},
                     "price_indices": {"IX": "4"}},
        }
        bid = compute(inputs)
        answer = bid["answer"]
        p1, p2 = answer["positions"]
        # pos 1: base 100*0.9 + surcharge 2*0.9 + (setup 10 + 2 cartons*6)/4 = 90 + 1.8 + 5.5
        self.assertEqual(p1["unit_price"], 97.30)
        self.assertEqual(p1["surcharge_per_unit"], 4.50)
        self.assertEqual(p1["packaging_per_unit"], 3.00)
        # pos 2: 6 pieces, default base-only: 90 + 2
        self.assertEqual((p2["quantity"], p2["unit_price"]), (6, 92.00))
        self.assertEqual(p1["lead_time_weeks"], 2)          # pooled demand 4 + 6 = 10 <= 10 free: from stock
        self.assertEqual(answer["total_net"], round(4 * 97.30 + 6 * 92.00, 2))
        self.assertEqual(answer["discount_percent"], 10.0)
        inputs["erp"]["stock"]["M-1"]["free"] = "9"           # not enough for both: all-or-nothing -> production
        self.assertEqual({p["lead_time_weeks"] for p in compute(inputs)["answer"]["positions"]}, {8})

cd /c/Users/crubs/Desktop/tum_hackathon/ehl-finale-template; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
MVP swarm: model-driven collection, analysts, bid calculator and signed submission

- Brief reader extracts reference, scenario date, bidder and authorised senders;
  site roles are resolved by the model at run time (swarm/sites.py).
- Scrapers (tender, spec, ERP, mail) browse with browser-use on their own CDP
  browser and save whole pages as evidence via read_page (iframes, closed
  details, tooltips, canvas labels, decoys skipped) plus fill_form for gates.
- Collection is a dataflow: analysts wait on done flags instead of phases;
  ERP work is a queue per catalogue group shared by up to three workers.
- Analysts extract JSON from saved pages (quantities with Q&A/withdrawals,
  current revision with amendments, mail authority/discount/conditions,
  ERP materials/conditions/stock) and match materials exactly.
- Bid calculator applies the brief's rules in Decimal (scales, FX, discount
  scope, setup pools, project bonus, packaging, lead times, one rounding).
- Submitter fills the tender-portal wizard and signs with the mail TAN.
- Sandbox robustness: Qwen without thinking and in JSON mode, no screenshots,
  longer browser timeouts, no browser-use about:blank animation (it loaded an
  external logo and hung the first navigation), stuck loads stopped and retried.
- Unit tests for normalisation, rules, pricing, matching and wiring.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log -1 --format='%H%n%B' | tail -6; git status --short | head

content.text:
The commit hasn't finished yet. `git commit` has been running since 18:12:50 because Entire's commit hook is still working, so `git log` still shows the old commit (`1734b68`). Everything is staged and nothing has been pushed. I've stopped here, as you asked.

**Commit message I used:** "MVP swarm: model-driven collection, analysts, bid calculator and signed submission". It covers 27 files (+2334 / −161):
- **Brief and sites:** a new agent reads the brief (tender reference, scenario date, bidder, who may approve what), and the model decides at run time which site is which.
- **Collecting:**
  - One browser agent per site (tender, spec, ERP, mail), each on its own browser.
  - They save whole pages as evidence, including iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips and text drawn on canvas.
  - A form helper fills access gates and the bid wizard.
  - The analysis agents start as soon as the data they need arrives.
  - The ERP lookups are split per catalogue group and shared by up to three workers.
- **Analysing:**
  - Quantities follow the latest bidder answer per position and ignore withdrawn ones.
  - Requirements come from the current spec revision, with its amendments applied.
  - Mails are checked for sender, exact reference and date.
  - Materials must match the requirements exactly.
- **Calculator:** applies the brief's rules (price scales, currency conversion, discount scope, setup pools, project bonus, packaging, lead times) and rounds once at the end.
- **Submitting:** fills the tender-portal wizard and signs the bid with the TAN from the webmail.
- **Sandbox fixes:**
  - Qwen runs without its reasoning pass and must answer in JSON.
  - No screenshots, and longer browser timeouts.
  - The browser-use loading animation is off; it caused today's tender-agent hang.
  - A stuck page load is stopped and retried once.
- **Tests:** unit tests for parsing, rules, pricing, matching and wiring; all 42 pass.

Before staging, I checked the package for scenario values; the only numbers found are in synthetic test data.

**The new test run** is going well: the tender agent finished in 25 steps, the quantities follow the bidder Q&A, the discount is 5%, and the spec agent picked the current revision.

To finish the commit: wait for the hook, or stop process `30232` and re-run the commit. Entire's `commit-msg` hook adds the checkpoint link on any normal `git commit`.

content.text:
The commit is stuck in Entire's git hook, not in git or in our code. Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` hook (the one that adds the checkpoint link to the message) hangs and never returns, so `git commit` waits on it forever.

**What I found:**
- **The hook process is idle.** It is `entire.exe hooks git prepare-commit-msg` (process 20096), started 18:12:50, and it hasn't written a single line to `.entire/logs/entire.log`.
- **It hangs every time.** I ran the same hook by hand on a throwaway message file, with no input attached. It printed nothing and was killed after 20 s, still hanging. So it isn't caused by the size of our commit or by how I called git.
- **An older hook is also still stuck.** A second `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg` (processes 9856 and 22284) has been hanging since **14:50:25**, about 3.5 hours. Its `git commit` is already gone, so that hook is orphaned. Hooks started after 14:53 still worked, so it didn't block everything straight away.
- **Probable cause:** the old hook holds some Entire lock, and every new hook waits for it. Less likely, the hook is waiting for an answer at a terminal prompt that this shell can't show. I haven't confirmed which one.

**Current state:**
- Nothing is committed yet; `HEAD` is still `1734b68`.
- All 27 files are staged.
- Entire itself works and is still saving session checkpoints (last one at 18:19:58), so linking will work once the hook stops hanging.

**Proposed fix (needs your OK):**
1. End the stuck processes: the old hook (9856 and 22284) and the current commit (30232, 2928, 29820, 20096).
2. Run the hook by hand again with a timeout. If it now returns, the old hook was blocking it, and I commit normally so Entire adds its checkpoint link.
3. If it still hangs, run `entire doctor`, which is meant to fix session issues, and try again.

Committing with `--no-verify` would skip the hook, but then the commit wouldn't be linked to Entire, so I won't do that. Should I go ahead?

**What was wrong:** Entire's hook (`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg`) hangs whenever it is started from the Git Bash shell I was using. It hung even when I ran it by hand on a test file. From PowerShell the same hook finishes in a few seconds and adds the checkpoint link. Entire's own check (`entire doctor`) reported nothing wrong, so it looks like a problem with Entire under Git Bash on Windows. I didn't find the exact cause, so I worked around it rather than repairing it.

**What I did:**
1. Ended all nine stuck processes: the hook that had been hanging since 14:50 and the commit from 18:12. No hook processes are left.
2. Made the commit from PowerShell, with a 90-second limit so it couldn't hang again.
3. Saved a note so I always commit from PowerShell in this repo, clear leftover hook processes first, and check the commit has its Entire link.

If you commit from your own terminal, PowerShell works; Git Bash may hang the same way.
